user.title: Observer location
user.description: Moon Astro computes the Moon position as seen from this location. The values are pre-filled from the Home Assistant configuration.

data_description.latitude: Geographic latitude in decimal degrees, positive north of the equator.
data_description.longitude: Geographic longitude in decimal degrees, positive east of Greenwich.
data_description.elevation: Height above sea level, in meters.

reconfigure.title: Observer location
reconfigure.description: Update the location used for the Moon position. Existing entities are kept.

data_description.latitude: Geographic latitude in decimal degrees, positive north of the equator.
data_description.longitude: Geographic longitude in decimal degrees, positive east of Greenwich.
data_description.elevation: Height above sea level, in meters.

progress.download_ephemeris: Downloading the JPL DE440 ephemeris (about 115 MB). This can take several minutes depending on your connection.

error.download_failed: The DE440 ephemeris could not be downloaded. Check that Home Assistant can reach ssd.jpl.nasa.gov, then try again.

init.title: Moon Astro options
init.description: Changes are applied when the integration reloads after saving.

data.use_ha_timezone: Use the Home Assistant time zone

data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between two computations of the current Moon position (60 to 21600). Shorter intervals increase CPU usage.
data_description.use_ha_timezone: Use the Home Assistant time zone for the calendar months that name full moons. Disable it to pick another zone below.
data_description.time_zone: IANA time zone used when the Home Assistant time zone is not used. Timestamps themselves are always published as UTC instants.
data_description.events_refresh_fallback: Seconds between two forced recomputations of the event-based sensors (3600 to 604800), in case the refresh scheduled after the next event is missed. 24 hours is plenty.

ephemeris_unavailable.message: The DE440 ephemeris is not available: {error}
